title: Control artifact chain-of-custody orchestrator for jurisdictional retention exports
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Background: Customers and auditors frequently request not just logs but forensically-verifiable evidence bundles that demonstrate control execution, retention policy enforcement, and geographic custody. Current exports produce CSVs and bulky audit bundles without cryptographic linking or clear retention lifecycle metadata. Goal: build an orchestrator that assembles append-only control artifacts into immutable export packages with cryptographic manifests, region/jurisdiction stamps, and retention lifecycle metadata so auditors can verify chain-of-custody and we can automate retention enforcement and legal-hold exceptions.

Scope:
- Collect evidence artifacts from Console, Runtime telemetry, and Dedicated agent snapshots for a given time window and jurisdiction.
- Produce an export package that contains: signed manifest (SHA256 hashes + HSM signature), Merkle-tree for bulk verification, human-friendly summary, and per-artifact retention metadata (jurisdiction, retention bucket, deletion ETA).
- Attach a tamper-evident envelope that records export operator identity, export time, and retention rules in force.
- Support incremental re-exports (deltas) and full snapshots.

Non-goals: live querying UI for auditors (we will provide downloadable packages and an audit validation CLI), long-term storage itself (leverages existing S3 buckets / customer-owned storage).

Success metrics:
- Auditor acceptance in two pilot customers (legal-inbound) within 6 weeks of launch.
- Export generation median latency < 3 minutes for 10k artifacts.
- Zero failed-verification reports in first 3 months after rollout.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- HSM-backed signing increases operational cost and complexity but gives stronger non-repudiation for enterprise customers. For lower tiers we will support software signing keys.
- Generating Merkle trees for very large artifact sets can be CPU-heavy; we'll limit single-package size by default and provide a sharded export mode.
- Jurisdictional stamping requires mapping runtime region metadata to legal jurisdictions; mapping gaps will be surfaced as warnings and require operator review.

Stakeholders: Compliance (primary), Runtime SRE, Dedicated infra, Product Security, Legal.

Open questions:
- Default package retention timeframe and retention bucket semantics for Dedicated customers.
- Export delivery patterns: direct S3 push to customer bucket vs Console download.

Recommended next steps: 1) finalize PRD and HSM cost estimate; 2) spike Merkle-tree generator on eng spike ticket; 3) run two customer pilots (EU fintech, NA SaaS) for feedback.
acceptance_criteria: Export packages include signed manifest referencing every artifact with SHA256 and HSM signature (or software fallback)
Each artifact entry has jurisdiction and retention_bucket metadata populated or marked as 'unknown' with a warning
Export validation CLI verifies package integrity using manifest and Merkle tree in <30s for up to 10k artifacts
Operator audit trail present in package (operator id, export timestamp, policy snapshot) and stored in Console event feed
Pilot customers can import package into auditor tooling and confirm chain-of-custody during pilot review
